note: Jephson Gardens deepen pass 2026-11-22. Source: Warwick District Council tree directory + 2024 tree-walk leaflet.

leads.name: Holm oak, last of the 1848 Ceremony of Oaks (Jephson Gardens)
leads.why: Council record (directory_record/17416) calls it the last of the oaks planted at the 1848 Ceremony of Oaks; says a much younger holm oak stands next to it nearer the main gate. Not shown to be a different tree from the lakeside holm oak felled 2025-07-15, so it may be gone. Needs a visit or a dated photo of a standing 1848 holm oak. Leaflet mark 92 points (west half) are 52.2870-52.2876, -1.5321 to -1.5327, unidentified.

leads.name: Silver pendant lime (Tilia tomentosa Petiolaris), by the lake path
leads.why: Council says view from the path by the lake; leaflet 110 has two marks (52.2877,-1.5331 and 52.2892,-1.5279), lake is near 52.2876,-1.5321, so neither pins it. Ordinary size evidence none. 2026-11-27 write pass: handed back unwritten, no pin it can honestly carry, no photo or recognition tell to tell it apart, and no size or age to say why it is worth the walk.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

leads.name: Deodar cedar possibly planted by Dr Hitchman
leads.why: Council record says "may have been" planted by Hitchman (late 1830s-40s). A prominent cedar near the Parade entrance and Hitchman Fountain was felled the week of 2024-10-14 (honey fungus, council notice 1234), likely the same tree; check before using.

leads.name: Coast redwood, Wellingtonia, Cedar of Lebanon, monkey puzzle, dawn redwood (Jephson Gardens)
leads.why: Council records give species notes only, no girth, size or position; wellingtonia record says it does not yet look that big; dawn redwood is mid-20th-century planting. Nothing a visitor can single out without a visit. 2026-11-25 write pass: handed back, five species in one row is not a single point; split it only when one of them has its own position and a reason to visit.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

blocked.name: Lakeside holm oak, UK Tree of the Year 2023 shortlist (Jephson Gardens)
blocked.reason: Felled by Warwick District Council on 2025-07-15 (basal decay, did not recover from pollarding; seating retained, replacement to be planted nearby), council news 1334 and Warwickshire World. Girth 5 m and about 175 years were its figures. Dead, never ship.
